summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to recurrent hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 43, accompanied by increased drainage and pain at her G-tube site. Imaging confirmed the G-tube was correctly positioned with no leakage, and contrast passed normally into the colon. She was restarted on metronidazole for small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, which may contribute to hypoglycemia. Granulation tissue at the G-tube site was treated with silver nitrate and mupirocin ointment. A fasting hypoglycemia work-up was completed, with labs drawn during a monitored fast before resuming feeds. She remained stable with blood glucose levels between 55 and 110, and was discharged home with new medications including octreotide and acarbose, instructions for wound care, and follow-up with her endocrinologist.
